To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we present the first lattice QCD calculation $\hat{q}(T)$ in (2+1) flavor of QCD.
we have carried out the first unquenching of the lattice QCD calculation for the transport coefficient $\hat q$.

the unquenched $\hat{q}/T^3$ in (2+1) flavor QCD plasma is found to increase monotonically with increasing temperature, and the value at the deconfinement transition temperature is $\hat{q}(T_c)/T_c^3 \approx 0.6 \text{ GeV}^2$.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the jet quenching parameter $\hat{q}(T)$ in QCD plasma.

the first unquenching lattice QCD calculation to determine the transport coefficient $\hat q$ of a thermal QGP medium, which is responsible for the modification of the parton's transverse momentum distribution.
the study of jet quenching, a phenomenon that has been observed in heavy-ion collisions at RHIC and LHC, where high transverse momentum partons are observed to be significantly suppressed.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the lattice-QCD calculation of the jet-quenching parameter $\hat{q}(T)$ is in reasonable agreement with the JET collaboration phenomenological extraction.
the lattice QCD calculation is consistent with the phenomenological analysis of jet quenching in heavy-ion collisions.

the calculated $\hat{g}$ and the phenomenologically extracted $\hat{q}/T^3$ are in reasonable agreement with each other, and hence, the leading-order process is the dominant process that controls the modification and suppression of high-$p_T$ jets in the heavy-ion collisions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the lattice QCD calculation is in agreement with the JET collaboration phenomenological extraction, and hence, the leading order perturbative calculation is valid in the temperature range considered here.
the lattice QCD calculations of $\hat{ q}$ are now mature enough to make a quantitative comparison to the data.
the lattice QCD calculation is able to reproduce the phenomenological $\hat{q}(T)$, and hence the phenomenology can be considered as a valid description of the jet quenching phenomenon.
The main takeaway from our work is that
$\hat{q}/T^3$ is nearly independent of the quark masses.
$\hat{q}(T)$ is a non-monotonic function of the temperature.
the leading-order contribution to $\hat{q}_{\text{glue}}$ is dominated by the contribution from the two-point function of gluon field-strength operators.
